name: Wild_Arcs

phase_0.boundary_condition: The point at infinity in the one-point compactification of ℝ³, which encodes the full knotting information of the wild arc's embedding class losslessly.

⊢.justification: The unknotted, tame arc before any wild embedding is imposed; the void state where no limit set complexity exists.

⊣.justification: The asymptotic boundary that contains the entire wild arc system; all topological information collapses to this terminal anchor.

≻.justification: The forward morphism building the wild arc through infinite iteration of knotted approximations converging to the limit set.

≺.justification: The reverse morphism attempting to undo the embedding by global isotopy of the sphere; fails for wild arcs due to high kinetic barriers.

⋈.justification: Sequential composition of tame approximating arcs whose limit yields the wild embedding; each link adds a stage of knotting.

⊙.justification: Self-recognition of the wild arc's topological type; the Alexander polynomial or winding invariant that knows itself.

∈.justification: At the critical phase, the embedding forks into wild and tame arms; arbitrarily small perturbations select the arm.

∋.justification: The two arms recombine at the point at infinity where the asymptotic boundary encodes both possibilities in the scale-collapse topology.

⊤.justification: The affirmative arm: the limit set is genuinely wild, not ambient isotopic to a tame arc.

⊥.justification: The negative arm: the limit set is tame, equivalent to a standard arc under ambient isotopy.

⊞.justification: At the exact critical threshold, the embedding holds both wild and tame character simultaneously; the paradice of scale-free sensitivity.

⊡.justification: Permanent fixation of the Alexander polynomial, winding number, or Fox-Artin invariant; append-only measurement that cannot be undone by isotopy.

phase_2.failure_reason: Tri-ancestral reconnection over a transformed object — closes

phase_3.void_description: No embedding defined; the ambient sphere contains only a trivial arc with no limit set complexity.
phase_3.true_description: Wild embedding class established; the limit set is not ambient isotopic to any tame arc.
phase_3.false_description: Tame embedding class established; the limit set is ambient isotopic to a standard arc.
phase_3.both_description: Critical threshold embedding where wild and tame characteristics coexist; the limit set exhibits scale-free correlations and maximal sensitivity.

steps.domain_action: Initialize the trivial arc in the ambient sphere before wildness is introduced.
The trivial arc recognizes its own tame embedding class.
Begin embedding progression — first knotted approximation added.
Compose second approximation onto the first; chain of tame arcs grows.
Third approximation; knotting complexity increases.
Chain composition continues; each link is a tame arc.
Self-reference at each finite stage — the approximation knows its own knot type.
Critical threshold reached — the infinite limit forks into wild and tame possibilities.
Wild arm — the limit set is genuinely wild (Fox-Artin type).
Wild arm continues — infinite iteration of knotting at smaller scales.
Wild arm self-recognizes its non-tame embedding class.
Tame arm — the limit set remains tame (standard arc).
Tame arm attempts isotopy retraction to trivial arc.
Tame arm self-recognizes its trivializability.
Limit set rejoining at infinity — both arms encoded in asymptotic boundary.
Critical embedding holds both wild and tame character simultaneously at threshold.

∈ (granularity): Global correlation — local change at any scale propagates to entire limit set.
∋ (interaction_grammar): Conjunctive partnership — arc and complement simultaneously required.
⊙ (criticality_phase): Critical threshold — scale-free correlations, maximal sensitivity.
⊥ (chirality): Topological chirality — mirror image not isotopic without global restructuring.
≻ (recognition_mode): Mechanical topology — irreversible interlocking with ambient space.
⋈ (fidelity): High fidelity — limit set topology enforces near-certain distinction.
⊡ (protection): Integer-winding protection — Alexander polynomial stable under isotopy.
Permanent record of topological invariant (Alexander polynomial) fixed in ROM.
Embedding class identity self-recognized at terminal boundary.
Point at infinity closes the system — all bulk information encoded in boundary.

phase_5.compiler_frontend: The infinite approximation sequence that translates finite tame arcs into the wild limit embedding.
phase_5.ipc_mechanism: Scale-collapse coupling — the boundary at infinity communicates with every scale of the limit set simultaneously.
phase_5.memory_mechanism: Topological invariants (Alexander polynomial, winding numbers) stored as integer-winding-protected ROM.
phase_5.scheduler_mechanism: Critical phase dynamics — the system operates at the threshold where arbitrarily small perturbations determine the embedding class.
phase_5.alfs_store: The Fox-Artin arc construction and its generalizations; the canonical wild arc bootstrap.

phase_6.cycle_cost: One global ambient isotopy per embedding class change.
phase_6.pre_cycle_state: Trivial arc in sphere; no limit set complexity.
phase_6.post_cycle_state: Wild arc with limit set encoding full knotting information at infinity.
phase_6.delta_s_verdict: ΔS ≈ 0 — The scale-collapse topology makes boundary and bulk information identical; the cycle conserves topological entropy.

grounding_reasoning:
⊣=𐑸: Wild arcs exhibit scale-collapse connectivity where knotting information is encoded entirely in the asymptotic boundary behavior at infinity.
⊢=𐑦: Wild arcs require scale-collapse dimensionality because their topological complexity is entirely captured by the embedding's behavior at infinity, making the boundary the sole carrier of bulk information.
⊞=𐑙: The embedding of a single wild arc in the ambient sphere constitutes an equal symmetric pairing between the arc and its complement.
⊡=𐑭: Wild arcs are integer-winding-protected because their topological invariants (e.g., Alexander polynomial, winding numbers) are stable against ambient isotopies preserving the embedding class.
⊙=⊙: Wild arcs exist at a critical threshold where arbitrarily small perturbations can change the embedding class, exhibiting scale-free complexity and maximal sensitivity at the limit point.
⊥=𐑫: Wild arcs exhibit topological chirality because their embedding classes (e.g., Fox-Artin arcs) are not ambient isotopic to their mirror images, requiring global restructuring of the ambient sphere to invert.
≻=𐑾: Wild arcs interact through mechanical topology where the embedding's knotted limit set creates irreversible interlocking with the ambient space that cannot be undone by local deformation.
≺=𐑗: The wild arc embedding possesses no inherent directional polarity or self-complementary interface; its complement in the sphere is topologically distinct but not organized by donor/acceptor roles.
⋈=𐑐: The wild arc's embedding class is a high-fidelity geometric invariant where the limit set topology enforces near-certain distinction between distinct wild embeddings.
⊤=𐑧: Wild arcs are kinetically frozen with high barriers because changing the embedding class requires global ambient isotopy of the sphere, not local deformation.
∈=𐑔: The wild arc's limit set creates scale-free correlations where a local embedding change propagates globally across the entire ambient sphere.
∋=𐑝: The wild arc embedding requires the simultaneous presence of the arc and its complement in the ambient sphere, forming a conjunctive partnership where both components are necessary to define the topological class.
